newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips erase gains at close.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips erase gains at close.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips erased modest gains by the close, as buying was sapped by the uncertainty over earnings and the prospect of weakness on Monday when DRB-Hicom stocks requote.

The Composite Index of 100 key stocks ended up 1.37 points to 1,251.21 after achieving a height of 1,253.13 during the session. The Second Board index of small-capitalised shares edged up 2.74 points to 650.05.
Share prices were consolidating, said Ralph Dixon of TA Securities' international division. "As a result of the high volume (recently), people have to pull in their reins."
Total volume was 400 million shares, versus 502 million on Thursday. Losers edged out gainers by 336 to 248.

Among key earnings reports the market is waiting for are Sime Darby, expected on Saturday. The conglomerate is expected to post half-year net profits of 424 million ringgit, versus 284.7 million a year ago, HG Asia estimated.

"The market is groping for direction," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at Capitalcorp. She said investors are "very keen" to see how Yahaya-linked stocks react when they are requoted. Nine stocks related to the late industrialist and to the DRB-Hicom group were suspended from Tuesday.
